measurement_scope.note: Synthetic local doubles and real production services; desktop timings are not Kodi, ARM, network, SMB/NFS or remote VFS promises. Counts and event ordering are authoritative where stated; repeated timings use medians and min/max ranges.

current_selector_execution.note: Active post-removal selectors plus the six-item discovery-root HTTP/lifecycle guard; all 30 were executed together in task-8-active-selectors.log. selector_execution above preserves the historical 40-selector pre-removal evidence; DB-only symbols and deleted test selectors are retained solely in historical_* / historical_removed_* fields.

live_verification.note: The following release changes only addon metadata and documentation; the verified runtime source is unchanged. No untested QR reauthentication or a paid media download was performed. ARM/NFS/SMB/remote-VFS latency was not measured.

benchmarks.kind: deterministic account/watchlist/genre request counters and complete cold saves

measured_result.summary: Warm one-page listing changed from one identity resolution plus one watchlist GET to zero of each. With an initially missing account ID, the second open still resolves /3/account once but reloads the resolved scope instead of repeating watchlist/genre work. Cold two-page fallback still performs two watchlist GETs and saves only after both validate; refresh queries and saved data retain the captured scope language.

comparisons.baseline: unmeasured: no matching baseline artifact cell

comparisons.operation: two opens with initially missing account

limitations: Remote changes are eventually visible after background completion and a later open; no live container refresh is generated by snapshot refresh.
Cold account/watchlist network work is intentionally retained and identity/generation mismatches reject stale writes.
A cold process may make one shared genre request independently; reservation and genre sharing are process-local.

benchmarks.kind: three real-filesystem runs per N and family, counting os.fsync and os.replace

measured_result.summary: For both trailer and show workers, 32 validated changes now cause four flushes rather than 32; N=8 causes one rather than eight, while N=1 remains one. Listing discovery uses one rather than two loads per used cache and submissions run after directory end.

limitations: On-demand writes remain immediate; deferred writes perform a locked reload/merge before the same atomic save.
Evidence counts persistence operations, not claimed elapsed-time or latency savings.

requirements.removal_scope: Backup DB storage and validation were retired; this requirement and its symbols/selectors are historical evidence only. Existing user database/text files and permanent backups were not migrated or deleted.

benchmarks.kind: 27 files by 500 items, seven repeated real-filesystem runs per operation

measured_result.summary: Historical removed Backup DB evidence: warm ensure plus one target load dropped from 55 data-document reads to one selected-file read and from 29.7032 ms to 9.8964 ms median on that offline run. This is not a claim about current production, which no longer contains the feature.

comparisons.operation: two is_valid calls after valid mtime-only drift

limitations: Only the warm matching-signature path avoids full parsing; migration and detected tamper deliberately retain full validation and are not claimed faster.
The signature is relative filename + size + mtime_ns; a content edit preserving both metadata fields is outside what this warm metadata check detects.
Separate before/after desktop timings are descriptive, not a controlled target-device latency promise.

requirements.scope: Media downloads only; the former cold Backup DB handoff measurements are retained below solely as historical removed-feature evidence.

benchmarks.kind: blocked event sequencing for media and cold DB; no sleeps or wall-clock acceptance gate

measured_result.summary: Current media invocation returns after accepted queue handoff before stream release; actual file success happens only after release and validated completion. Worker-start failure removes only the unaccepted reservation/status and permits retry, while each independent worker session clones the main session headers without sharing the session object. Cold DB rows are historical measurements from before Backup DB removal.

comparisons.operation: historical removed cold DB stream blocked
historical removed concurrent cold DB open

comparisons.unit: post-promotion refreshes / warm reopen new auth calls

limitations: Acceptance is not remote success. No throughput or latency speedup is inferred from event ordering.
One process-local queue permits four running+queued jobs; close is cooperative and cannot forcibly interrupt an OS-blocked socket call.
Remote VFS rename atomicity remains backend-dependent.

requirements.scope: The static root remains authentication-free without Backup DB. Retired db/searchdb bookmarks use the same ordinary root fallback without auth, network, client methods or user-data/database reads.

benchmarks.kind: deterministic revalidate/_post request counters and unchanged rendered route counts

measured_result.summary: Four Webshare static menu items render with zero revalidation/auth and zero explicit remote calls. The combined pre-discovery root had five items after Backup DB retirement; the integrated root now has six with Objevit first, still without discovery HTTP or background jobs. Retired db/searchdb bookmarks exactly match that current ordinary unknown-action root fallback, complete once and do not call auth/token/client methods, network or user-data/database reads.

comparisons.operation: static Webshare main menu after retirement
historical removed installed DB queue action

limitations: Media, search and remote queue operations still validate at point of use; the static root performs no authentication.

measured_result.summary: A 100-key direct submission now covers all 100 keys exactly once in four <=32-key batches rather than silently dropping IDs 33-100. The gain is complete bounded draining and deduplication, not fewer total requests.

comparisons.current: 100, one per key in alternating family order

comparisons.unit: HTTP attempts / persisted successful rows / negative rows
comparisons.current: 132 / 68 / 0; exactly 2 attempts for IDs 1-32 and 1 for 33-100

limitations: Making 100 rather than 32 calls is intentional completeness, not evidence of reduced network traffic or lower latency.
Each UI open schedules only the first 50 visible rows per family; all rows still render and on-demand lookup remains available.
One worker and process-local shared flights remain the lifecycle/concurrency boundary.

benchmarks.kind: actual production canonical helper versus exact legacy membership loop, seven actual-helper timing runs per H

measured_result.summary: Canonical whole-content keys improve the H=1000 helper median from 8.1065 ms to 4.6235 ms (1.753x), while H=20 and H=200 are slower because of canonical allocation. Blank/missing/unknown-ID removal makes one history GET rather than two without changing rendered rows; valid-ID clear then reload remains unchanged.

comparisons.unit: history GETs / clear requests / rendered rows

limitations: Small history H=20/200 canonical allocation is measurably slower; linear memory keys also increased separate single-run tracemalloc peaks at H=1000 from 4296 to 451336 bytes.
The full history handler is not claimed faster: Task 6 instrumented whole-handler medians increased despite the actual-helper H=1000 improvement.
Canonical semantics retain full dictionary equality, container kind/order, duplicate data and first object occurrence rather than lossy ID/name deduplication.

requirements.removal_scope: Backup DB archive ingestion was retired with the feature; media stream_download and its unchanged media requirements remain active. This requirement is historical evidence only.

benchmarks.kind: stream/validation counters, cold timing and sequential JSON member memory evidence

measured_result.summary: Historical removed Backup DB evidence: archive ingestion used an owned same-profile seekable temporary file at 262144-byte chunks, with zero response.content accesses or production whole-archive BytesIO copies. This archive path is absent from current production; media stream_download remains active under PERF-09.

comparisons.unit: whole-response content reads / production whole-archive BytesIO copies
largest member / traced validation peak / chunk bytes

limitations: Streaming removes whole-archive copies but mandatory json.load() still buffers one JSON member and its object graph at a time; total memory is not bounded independently of the largest JSON member.
tracemalloc is not RSS and excludes native buffers; cold install/migration is not claimed faster.
The benchmark's byte-loader path cannot model live network memory or throughput.

benchmarks.kind: actual stream_download, local and bounded VFS double, 1/8/64 MiB, three repetitions per cell with byte and SHA-256 checks

measured_result.summary: The selected 256 KiB default deterministically gives 4x fewer full-write calls than 64 KiB with identical hashes. Current-session 64-vs-256 medians favor 256 KiB in five of six cells; local 1 MiB is a measured exception (4.1846 vs 4.0230 ms), so no universal timing win is claimed.

comparisons.operation: VFS double 1 MiB with 32 KiB partial writes

limitations: Traced peaks rise with chunk size and partial-write slicing; the larger synthetic 1024 KiB cells are not justification to exceed the approved conservative default.
Only synthetic local/VFS-double data was measured. Real Kodi, ARM, NFS/SMB and remote VFS throughput or memory improvement remains unverified.
The deterministic improvement is write-call reduction with identical data, not a blanket latency guarantee.
